newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs start to pick up after torpor.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs start to pick up after torpor.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carrier (VLCC) rates picked up on Wednesday, ending their recent torpor induced partly by Asian refinery maintenance, brokers said.
They said there was severe tightness for prompt dates, but even for later loadings rates had firmed to most destinations from the Middle East in an active market.
"Rates are definitely moving up. For prompt dates there's not much tonnage around but from 20th (May) onwards you should find a ship," one broker said.
He put Mideast VLCC rates at W50, up from a low of W45 last week, but said W57.5-60 was feasible for a prompt modern ship.
There was also a firmer tone on West Africa VLCCs, which were fixed around W65, against W62.5 last week although they remain well below their year high of about W75, brokers said.
Million barrel (130,000 tonne) West Africa/USAC rates were pegged at about W95, with Mediterranean cargoes at about the same level.
Med 80,000 tonne vessels fetched W110 or slightly more in a date-sensitive market. "One day earlier or later can make all the difference," one broker said.
European fuel oil was unchanged with 25,000 tonnes at W185 in the north and W195 in the Med.
In the Caribs/upcoast market, 70,000 tonnes of crude was unchanged at around W185, while 50,000 tonnes of fuel oil was firmer at W182.5, brokers said.
